A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HUMANML3D++ dataset and TAAT framework despite the changed title. All ten pages of each PDF, including figures, tables, equations, and references, support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix or embedded supplement.

before.justification: v4 reports original motion-generation and zero-shot experiments, filtering and prompt ablations, index-length analysis, and a human evaluation of generated motions.

after.justification: v5 retains original motion-generation experiments and ablations and adds a human-rated comparison of LLMs used to generate scene annotations.

M1.justification: Section 3 revises the reported data-construction pipeline to include an independent LLM that checks generated annotations, beyond v4's rule-based filtering and human review. The TAAT generator retains its LoRA-tuned Think model, VQ-VAE, and autoregressive ACT procedure; expanded conditioning notation and stopping explanations do not establish a different generator.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Action Text to Motion on HUMANML3D, Scene Text to Motion on HUMANML3D++, and zero-shot transfer between these settings. Annotation generation was already evaluated through prompt ablations, so the additional LLM comparison and scene examples do not introduce a new task or domain.

E2.justification: New Table 6 compares GPT-3.5, GPT-4o, and Llama-3-8B with the selected Gemini annotation generator. The TAAT-versus-T2M-GPT motion user study is removed. The five motion-generation baselines in Tables 3 and 4 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v5 adds an annotation evaluation using 100 scene texts and 23 assessors, while removing the motion study using 100 Scene Texts, 100 Action Texts, and 30 participants. It reduces the reported metric suites in Tables 2 and 4 and changes the stated data-validation stopping rule from resolving all detectable errors to exceeding 95% accuracy. Newly disclosed LLM training settings do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v5 adds analysis of annotation-generator choice and multiple-response scene case studies in Figure 6, while removing v4's perceptual motion evaluation in Section 6.5 and Figure 6. The filtering, prompt-design, and index-length ablations remain, with the latter two matched across renumbering.

E5.justification: Shared results retain the same plus-or-minus reporting. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence levels, or significance tests. Added rating percentages and removed metric columns change reported results, without establishing a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 3 and the retained entries in Table 4 are numerically unchanged. v5 removes Table 2's FID results, Table 4's MM-Dist and MModality results, and the motion-user-study outcomes. It adds scene examples and annotation ratings, including Gemini's 23.5% excellent, 75.9% suitable, and 0.6% inappropriate results in Table 6; these are new outcomes, not motion-performance improvements.

T1.justification: The rewritten conditioning expressions make the previously described Think-to-ACT composition explicit. The motion-generation recurrence and Hit Accuracy/Mean Hit Distance definitions remain substantively unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs that are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: introducing arbitrary-text motion generation, HUMANML3D++, the Think-and-Act framework, and multi-solution evaluation. The new title and more concrete descriptions of reactive motions do not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: v5 adds a question-answering analogy for the metrics and a quality-versus-cost rationale for choosing Gemini, while removing the action-generation discussion attributing diffusion failures to noise and lack of discretization. Section 5 also recasts the unchanged scene R-Precision of 0.665 as a misjudgment rate approaching 40%, without explaining that approximation.

D1.justification: Reproducibility documentation changes substantially. v5 supplies a fine-tuning instruction/example, identifies LLaMA and Gemini, and reports LLM training limits, optimizer settings, validation allocation, LoRA rank 8, and batch size 16. Conversely, it removes v4's VQ-VAE codebook dimensions, downsampling rate, training schedule, and loss weights. Both retain only a promise to release data, model, and code.

R1.justification: v5 adds AvatarGPT as reference 50 and cites it among text-conditioned motion-generation works. The other cited works and the principal positioning against existing motion-generation approaches remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Beyond the title change, substantial passages in the introduction, dataset construction, method, metrics, and experimental interpretation are rewritten. The experimental narrative is reordered from Action Text, zero-shot, and Scene Text experiments to Scene Text, Action Text, and zero-shot experiments, placing the new task first.

P2.justification: v5 adds a fine-tuning-example figure, a multiple-response scene montage, and an LLM comparison table, and removes the motion-user-study chart. Tables 2 and 4 lose columns, with Table 4 becoming a single-column display. Existing qualitative comparisons and the index-length plot are retained across restyling, relocation, and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v5 improves explanation of the task and LLM training and adds useful evidence about annotation-generator choice. However, it removes the motion user study, informative action-generation metrics, and VQ-VAE training details. These changes improve documentation and dataset assessment while weakening motion validation and another part of reproducibility. The unchanged benchmark results do not resolve this tradeoff sufficiently to establish a reliable net improvement or deterioration.
